citation: Edwin O. Gale, Reminiscences of Early Chicago and Vicinity (Chicago: Fleming H. Revell Company, 1902), printed pp. 25, 43 and 51.
author: Edwin O. Gale
describes_date: Town walk framed by arrival on 25 May 1835; retrospective recollection published in 1902.
repository: Internet Archive, item reminiscencesofe00ingale; Allen County Public Library digitized volume
locator: Printed p 25 / service n 40 gives arrival 25 May 1835; Chapter III begins the town walk on printed p 43 / n 66; printed p 51 / n 76 describes the original Tremont. Actual title n 12 and copyright n 13 establish the 1902 imprint.
rights_note: US-published 1902 text, out of copyright by age. Actual title and copyright pages of this volume were inspected; this finding concerns the book text, not the separate undated Gifford drawing or a later reproduction.
note:
The actual uncropped scans of printed pp 25,43,51 were read. On p 51 Gale writes: "On the northwest corner of Lake and Dearborn streets is Chicago's sixth hotel, the original 20 x 30 yellow two story Tremont House, built in 1833 by Alanson Sweet, with Starr Foot as first proprietor." The arrival and chapter context frame the walk in 1835; this is a participant recollection published 67 years later, not a contemporary survey. Feet are a contextual unit inference: the printed 20 x 30 does not spell out a unit or identify its axes. The optional Gale interpretation takes 30 ft along the existing long axis and 20 ft along the short axis, with a rectangular plan; precise conversion does not imply survey precision. Yellow is adopted as inferred for the primary reconstruction; the smaller two-storey interpretation remains an optional native version, explicitly contrary to the pictured three-storey shuttered form. Gifford's undated drawing genuinely depicts three storeys; neither source dates an enlargement, so no enlargement chronology is invented.

CURRENT USE, 2026-10-26: this is textual recollection, not a second picture of the hotel. Its yellow description supplies inferred colour compatible with the monochrome Gifford drawing. Its smaller dimensions and two-storey count remain explicit contrary evidence, preserved in the optional gale-reading native version; they no longer replace the pictured three-storey shuttered primary form. No enlargement date or exact July1835 resolution is inferred from that disagreement.
what_it_supplies: A retrospective, 1835-framed account identifying the original Tremont at the northwest Lake and Dearborn corner, built 1833 by Alanson Sweet.
The printed description original20x30 yellow two story: compatible inferred colour for the primary pictured form, with dimensions/storeys retained as a contrary optional textual interpretation.
Starr Foot named as first proprietor, without a precise tenure date.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surveyed plan, explicit units or long/short axis orientation, wall heights, exact yellow pigment, dated roof or opening details.
A dated construction alteration reconciling the two-storey text with the three-storey Gifford depiction.
Proof that every detail remembered in 1902 was present on 1 July 1835.
